headline: Denied storage variances at 131 High Range Road; approved an accessory dwelling unit at 5 Wilson Road and garage variances at 2 Old Nashua Road.
summary: Nathan Stiller and Jacquelyn White were denied permission for an additional portable storage container and for storing heavy equipment at 131 High Range Road. Each vote was 5-0.

plain_text:
TOWN OF LONDONDERRY 
ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT MEETING
MOOSE HILL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
268B MAMMOTH ROAD
AUGUST 19, 2026, 7:00 P.M.
DRAFT MINUTES
CALL TO ORDER
Members Present: Jacqueline Benard, Chair; Suzanne Brunelle, Vice Chair; Brendan O'Brien,
Clerk; Mitchell Feig, Member; Lisa Sussman, Alternate Member; Ariana McQuarrie, Alternate
Member; Andria Hansen, Alternate Member
Members Absent: Greg Carson, Member
Also Present: Nick Codner, Chief Building Inspector/Zoning Administrator
Chair Benard called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and reviewed the meeting procedure. 
ROLL CALL
APPROVAL OF DRAFT MINUTES 
S. Brunelle moved to accept the minutes of the July 15, 2026, meeting as written. B. O'Brien
seconded the motion. The motion carried 4-0-0.
REPORT BY TOWN COUNCIL LIAISON
There was no report by the Town Council liaison. 
REGIONAL IMPACT DETERMINATIONS
Staff determined that none of the cases being heard were of regional impact.
B. O'Brien moved to accept the regional impact determination. M. Feig seconded the motion.
The motion carried 4-0-0.
PUBLIC HEARING OF CASES
Case No. 07-15-2026-5 - Request For A Variance From LZO 5.15.A.1 To Allow An Additional
Portable Storage Structure In The Agricultural Residential-1 (AR-1) Zoning District. The
Property Is Located At 131 High Range Road, Tax Map 6, Lot 5-1. Nathan Stiller And
Jacquelyn White, Owner/Applicant (continued from July 15, 2026)
Chair Benard appointed Andria Hansen as a full voting member for this case. 
B. O'Brien read the case into the record. 
Nathan Stiller and Jacquelyn White appeared before the Board to continue discussion of their
request to allow a portable storage container on their property. The Board reviewed information
regarding the special exception granted on December 19, 1995, to operate an auto repair
business as a home occupation. This is be the second container on the property, used to store
shovels, snow/ice hand tools, and snowblowers. It will serve as temporary storage. 
Chair Benard asked for public comment.
Mark Greenwood, 133 High Range Road, spoke in support of the request.  
B. O'Brien read letters into the record from Peter Norton, 116 High Range Road, and Yvette
and Donna Hicks, 123 High Range Road, in support of the request. 
Chair Benard reported receiving a letter on July 15, 2026, in opposition to the request. B.
O'Brien read the letter from Jake Butler, 2 Danbury Court, into the record. 
N. Stiller said he was unaware of the zoning ordinance when he placed the container on the
property, and was willing to replace it with a structure that met the ordinance. 
Chair Benard closed the public portion of the hearing and the Board began deliberation.
B. O'Brien reviewed the variance criteria:
1) Granting the variance would not be contrary to the public interest because the proposal
would not alter the character of the neighborhood. The vote was 4-1.
2) The spirit of the ordinance would be observed because the proposal does not threaten public
health, safety, or general welfare. 
3) Granting the variance would do substantial justice, as denying the variance would result in a
greater loss to the applicant than any gain to the public. 
4) The values of the surrounding properties would not be diminished because of the location
and size of the container.
5) Owing to special conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the
area, denial of the variance would result in an unnecessary hardship because:
(a) for purposes of this subparagraph, "unnecessary hardship" means that, owing to special
conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the area, 
(i) there is a fair and substantial relationship between the general public purposes of the
ordinance provision and the specific application of that provision to the property because the
property is not unique.
(ii) the proposed use is not a reasonable one.
B. O'Brien moved in Case No. 07-15-2026-5 to deny the request for a variance. A. Hansen
seconded the motion. The motion carried 5-0-0.
Case No. 07-15-2026-6 - Request For A Variance From LZO 4.1 To Allow The Storage Of
Heavy Equipment In The Agricultural Residential-1 (AR-1) Zoning District. The Property Is
Located At 131 High Range Road, Tax Map 6, Lot 5-1. Nathan Stiller And Jacquelyn White,
Owner/Applicant (continued from July 15, 2026)
B. O'Brien read the case into the record. 
Chair Benard appointed Andria Hansen as a full voting member for this case. 
Nathan Stiller and Jacquelyn White appeared before the Board to discuss this request to allow
storage of vehicles and light equipment for snow removal on their property. N. Stiller said per
the NHDMV, anything under 26,000 GVW is not considered commercial equipment. He plans
to store pickup trucks, small skid steer bobcats, and small wheel loaders, all of which are under
26,000 GVW. 
The Board asked how much equipment would be stored at one time. N. Stiller said it could be
limited to ten pieces. He would like to store the equipment in a cleared area in the woods to be
able to use the garage for his personal use. 
J. White reviewed the variance criteria. 
The Board asked about maintaining equipment. N. Stiller said this could include oil changes
and greasing of machinery, which would be done inside the garage. 
Chair Benard asked for public comment. 
Mark Greenwood, 133 High Range Road, spoke in support of the request, noting that the
equipment is currently onsite and is not an eyesore.
B. O'Brien noted that the three letters read into the record in Case No. 07-15-2026-5 applied to
this case as well. 
Chair Benard closed the public portion of the hearing and the Board began deliberation. B.
O'Brien noted the prior zoning action contained restrictions: no more than five vehicles at any
time and no storage of vehicles overnight. It also contained provisions for fluid removal. Chair
Benard noted the previous case allowed for a minimal effect on the neighborhood; the Board at
that time agreed that the neighborhood should not look commercial, and the look and feel of
the property should not change. 
B. O'Brien reviewed the variance criteria:
1) Granting the variance would be contrary to the public interest because storing equipment in
this amount and of this size is not what is normally seen in a residential neighborhood, and
would change the character.
2) The spirit of the ordinance would not be observed because the presence of equipment and
the associated fluids/chemicals would threaten public health, safety, or general welfare. 
3) Granting the variance would not do substantial justice as granting it would result in a greater
loss to the general public than any gain to the applicant, due to the change in the neighborhood
and the threat to safety due to the increase in potential hazardous waste. 
4) The values of the surrounding properties would be diminished because the variance goes
with the land, and the surrounding properties would be impacted if future property owners were
not good stewards of the land. Three Board members felt the vote was close, noting that no
problems have occurred so far and the storage is out of sight. 
5) Owing to special conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the
area, denial of the variance would result in an unnecessary hardship because:
(a) for purposes of this subparagraph, "unnecessary hardship" means that, owing to special
conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the area, 
(i) there is a fair and substantial relationship between the general public purposes of the
ordinance provision and the specific application of that provision to the property because the
property is not unique. 
(ii) the proposed use is not a reasonable one because this type of equipment should not be
stored on a residential property. 
B. O'Brien moved in Case No. 07-15-2026-6 to deny the request for a variance for the reasons
stated on the record and on the voting sheet. S. Brunelle seconded the motion. The motion
carried 5-0-0.
Case No. 08-19-2026-1 Request For A Variance From LZO 5.18.H.2 To Allow An Accessory
Dwelling Unit (ADU) To Be Located Within The Front Yard Of The Property. LZO 5.18.H.2
Requires An ADU To Be Located Within The Side Or Rear Yard Of The Property In The
Agricultural Residential-1 (AR-1) District. The Property Is Located At 5 Wilson Road, Tax Map
16, Lot 012-0. David And Karen Kelly (Owner) And Jeremy Cable (Applicant).
S. Brunelle recused herself from this case. Chair Benard appointed Andria Hansen and Lisa
Sussman as full voting members for this case. 
B. O'Brien read the case into the record. 
Jeremy Cable, builder, appeared before the Board to discuss this request to construct an ADU
in the Kellys' front yard. He noted the house is perpendicular to and 250 yards from the road,
so the front yard is not located on the main road. He described the property, including the
location of other structures and the topography. 
J. Cable read the variance criteria. 
Chair Benard asked for public comment.
Karen Kelly, 5 Wilson Road, explained she and her husband would like to construct the ADU
for their adult daughter, so she can help care for her parents.  
Chair Benard closed the public portion of the hearing and the Board went into deliberation. 
B. O'Brien reviewed the variance criteria:
1) Granting the variance would not be contrary to the public interest because the proposal does
not alter the character of the neighborhood. 
2) The spirit of the ordinance would be observed because the proposal does not threaten public
health, safety, or general welfare. 
3) Granting the variance would do substantial justice, as denying it would result in a greater
loss to the applicant than any gain to the public. 
4) The values of surrounding properties would not be diminished. 
5) Owing to special conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the
area, denial of the variance would result in an unnecessary hardship because:
(a) for purposes of this subparagraph, "unnecessary hardship" means that, owing to special
conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the area, 
(i) there is not a fair and substantial relationship between the general public purposes of the
ordinance provision and the specific application of that provision to the property because it is a
unique property, given the size, distance of the home from the road, location of the well, hill
behind the home, and placement of the house.  
(ii) the proposed use is a reasonable one, as ADUs are reasonable. 
B. O'Brien moved in Case No. 08-19-2026-1 to grant the request for a variance. L. Sussman
seconded the motion. The motion carried 5-0-0.
Case No. 08-19-2026-2 Request For A Variance From LZO 4.3.3.A.1 To Allow A Commercial
Garage To Encroach 46 Feet Into The Required 60-Foot Front Setback In The Commercial 1
(C-1) District. The Property Is Located At 2 Old Nashua Road, Map 3, Lot 131-1. 16 Maple St.,
LLC (Owner/Applicant)
B. O'Brien read the case into the record. 
S. Brunelle returned to the Board. Chair Benard appointed Andria Hansen as a full voting
member for this case. 
Dan Borowski, Fieldstone Land Consultants, appeared before the Board representing the
applicant to present this request to construct a structure containing four contractor bays and to
utilize the existing building as office space for tenants. In response to the Board's questions, he
described the rationale for the location in terms of minimizing the impact on Route 102 and
ease of access for the tenants. N. Codner noted the existing building was a former restaurant
with a septic system large enough to support that business. 
Chair Benard asked for public comment; there was none. 
D. Borowski read the variance criteria. 
Chair Benard closed the public portion of the hearing and the Board went into deliberation.
They discussed whether another business could operate in this location without encroaching on
the setback, but acknowledged that the structure had been vacant for a while. They noted there
was previous zoning action on the property in 1972, but no details were available about it. 
B. O'Brien reviewed the variance criteria:
1) Granting the variance would not be contrary to the public interest because the proposal
would not alter the essential character of the neighborhood. 
2) The spirit of the ordinance would be observed because the proposal does not threaten public
health, safety, or general welfare. 
3) Granting the variance would do substantial justice, as not granting it would result in a greater
loss to the applicant than any gain to the public. 
4) The values of surrounding properties would not be diminished, as it is a commercial district
and the property is adjacent to Route 102.
5) Owing to special conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the
area, denial of the variance would result in an unnecessary hardship because:
(a) for purposes of this subparagraph, "unnecessary hardship" means that, owing to special
conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the area, 
(i) there is not a fair and substantial relationship between the general public purposes of the
ordinance provision and the specific application of that provision to the property because it is a
corner lot on Route 102 in a commercial district with multiple setbacks, so is unique.
(ii) the proposed use is a reasonable one, as a business, garage, and office are reasonable. 
B. O'Brien moved in Case No. 08-19-2026-2 to grant the request for a variance. S. Brunelle
seconded the motion. The motion carried 5-0-0.
Case No. 08-19-2026-3 Request For A Variance From LZO 4.3.3.A.2 To Allow A Commercial
Garage To Encroach 15 Feet Into The Required 30-Foot Side Setback In The Commercial 1
(C-1) District. The Property Is Located At 2 Old Nashua Road, Map 3, Lot 131-1. 16 Maple St.,
LLC (Owner/Applicant).
B. O'Brien read the case into the record. 
Chair Benard accepted that Case 08-19-2026-3 and all the five points of law have already been
taken into the record, as they are exactly the same as in Case 08-19-2026-2.
Dan Borowski, Fieldstone Land Consultants, appeared before the Board representing the
applicant to present this request. He noted that the rationale he presented for Case
08-19-2026-2 were exactly the same for this case.
Chair Benard asked for public comment; there was none. 
Chair Benard closed the public portion of the hearing and the Board went into deliberation. 
B. O'Brien reviewed the variance criteria:
1) Granting the variance would not be contrary to the public interest because the proposal
would not alter the essential character of the neighborhood. 
2) The spirit of the ordinance would be observed because the proposal does not threaten public
health, safety, or general welfare.
3) Granting the variance would do substantial justice, as not granting it would result in a greater
loss to the applicant than any gain to the public. 
4) The values of surrounding properties would not be diminished, as it is a commercial district
and the property is adjacent to Route 102.
5) Owing to special conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the
area, denial of the variance would result in an unnecessary hardship because:
(a) for purposes of this subparagraph, "unnecessary hardship" means that, owing to special
conditions of the property that distinguish it from other properties in the area, 
(i) there is not a fair and substantial relationship between the general public purposes of the
ordinance provision and the specific application of that provision to the property because it is a
corner lot on Route 102 in a commercial district with multiple setbacks, so is unique.
(ii) the proposed use is a reasonable one, as a business, garage, and office are reasonable. 
B. O'Brien moved in Case No. 08-19-2026-3 to grant the request for a variance. M. Feig
seconded the motion. The motion carried 5-0-0.
COMMUNICATION AND MISCELLANEOUS
OTHER BUSINESS
ADJOURN
S. Brunelle moved to adjourn the meeting. M. Feig seconded the motion. The motion carried
5-0-0.  
The meeting was adjourned at 8:47 p.m.
Respectfully submitted,
Beth Hanggeli
Recording Secretary
